text:
The Canucks are 5-18-1 with 11 points, and Manny Malhotra's first season behind the bench has turned into a rebuild out loud. They've had 39% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, so this isn't a lucky team having a bad month. Our numbers give them no realistic path to the playoffs.

The goaltending has made it worse. Kevin Lankinen has lost his last five starts with an .802 save rate, 9.3 goals worse than an average goalie would allow on the same shots. Our numbers say the Canucks have about five fewer points than their play has earned, which tells you how far below even the bad baseline they've fallen.

Elias Pettersson is the story everyone's writing: trade talk has picked up, with Elliotte Friedman among the voices reporting a new turn. His line with Jake DeBrusk and Jonathan Lekkerimäki has had only 42% of the chances. Brock Boeser, meanwhile, is getting written up as a captain in waiting. Filip Chytil scored twice in the 6-3 win that ended a seven-game losing streak.

The worry is the blue line. Filip Hronek and Zeev Buium have had 32% of the chances together, and the Kraken put 43 shots on them Thursday, 24 in the first period alone. Tom Willander has drawn praise as one of the most impactful skaters on the team. For the rest of this season, we'd judge it on the kids, not the standings.
headline: A rebuild, a captain's case and Pettersson talk
